ai_explanation.concept_rule: The sine rule states that $\frac{a}{\sin A} = \frac{b}{\sin B}$.
step_by_step: Pair the side $x$ with the opposite angle $27^\circ$, and $16$ with $31^\circ$.
Equate the ratios using the sine rule.
Rearrange to solve for $x$ and evaluate.

mark_breakdown.desc: Finding the third angle of the triangle
Setting up the sine rule equation

subparts.solution: $\text{B}\widehat{\text{A}}\text{C} = 180^\circ - 57^\circ - 83^\circ = 40^\circ$ (angles in a triangle). Now by the sine rule: $\frac{x}{\sin 83^\circ} = \frac{3.5}{\sin 40^\circ} \implies x = \frac{3.5\sin 83^\circ}{\sin 40^\circ} \approx 5.40$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: When a side is given opposite an unknown angle, first use the angle sum of a triangle ($180^\circ$) before applying the sine rule.
step_by_step: Multiply both sides by $\sin 83^\circ$ and compute.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Using the wrong angle opposite to $3.5\text{ km}$.
